provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Pre-writing strokes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify sleeping lines.
The pupils should be able to draw standing lines.

Introduction:
Last week we played with pencils.
Today we learn to draw lines.

Content:
Sleeping lines are horizontal lines like a sleeping snake.
Standing lines are vertical lines like a tall tree.
Slanting lines go from left to right like a hill.

Class activity:
Pupils use their fingers to draw lines in the air.
Then they draw lines on sand.

Evaluation questions:
Show me a sleeping line.
Draw a standing line.
Which line looks like a hill?

Summary:
We can draw many different lines.

topics.title: Curves and circles
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw circles.
The pupils should be able to trace half circles.

Introduction:
Last week we drew straight lines.
Today we learn curves and circles.

Content:
A circle is a round shape with no corners.
Big circles are like a big pot.
Small circles are like coins.
Half circles look like a rainbow.

Class activity:
Pupils draw big circles in the air with their arms.
Then they trace half circles on paper.

Evaluation questions:
Draw a big circle.
Trace a small circle.
What shape is like a rainbow?

Summary:
Circles have no corners.

topics.title: Patterns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to trace zigzag patterns.
The pupils should be able to colour wave patterns.

Introduction:
Last week we drew circles.
Today we learn patterns.

Content:
A zigzag pattern goes up and down like a mountain.
A wave pattern goes up and down like water.
Patterns are fun to make and colour.

Class activity:
Pupils trace zigzag lines on paper.
Then they colour wave patterns with crayons.

Evaluation questions:
Show me a zigzag pattern.
Colour a wave pattern.
What pattern looks like a mountain?

Summary:
Patterns are made of repeated shapes.

topics.title: Writing 1 and 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to trace number 1.
The pupils should be able to trace number 2.

Introduction:
Last week we made patterns.
Today we learn to write numbers.

Content:
Number 1 is a straight line like a stick.
Number 2 has a curve and a slant like a swan.
We write numbers from top to bottom.

Class activity:
Pupils trace number 1 in sand.
Then they trace number 2 on paper.

Evaluation questions:
Trace number 1.
Trace number 2.
Which number looks like a swan?

Summary:
We can write numbers 1 and 2.

topics.title: Writing 3 and 4
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to trace number 3.
The pupils should be able to trace number 4.

Introduction:
Last week we wrote numbers 1 and 2.
Today we learn numbers 3 and 4.

Content:
Number 3 has two curves like a butterfly.
Number 4 has a straight line and a triangle.
We write numbers neatly in the lines.

Class activity:
Pupils trace number 3 in the air.
Then they write number 4 in their books.

Evaluation questions:
Trace number 3.
Write number 4.
Which number looks like a butterfly?

Summary:
We can write numbers 3 and 4.

topics.title: Writing 5
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to trace number 5.
The pupils should be able to count to five.

Introduction:
Last week we wrote numbers 3 and 4.
Today we learn number 5.

Content:
Number 5 has a curve and a straight line.
We can count five fingers.
We can write number 5 neatly.

Class activity:
Pupils count five objects in class.
Then they trace number 5 on paper.

Evaluation questions:
Trace number 5.
Count to five.
Show me five fingers.

Summary:
Number 5 is easy to write.

topics.title: Tracing Aa to Ee
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to trace letters A to E.
The pupils should be able to say each sound.

Introduction:
Last week we wrote number 5.
Today we learn letters A to E.

Content:
Letter A is like a triangle with a line.
Letter B has two curves like spectacles.
Letter C is like a half circle.
Letter D has a curve and a straight line.
Letter E has three lines and a curve.

Class activity:
Pupils trace letters on sand.
Then they say each sound together.

Evaluation questions:
Trace letter A.
Say the sound of B.
Which letter looks like spectacles?

Summary:
We can trace letters A to E.

topics.title: Tracing Ff to Jj
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to trace letters F to J.
The pupils should be able to write on their own.

Introduction:
Last week we traced letters A to E.
Today we learn letters F to J.

Content:
Letter F has two lines and a curve.
Letter G has a curve and a small line.
Letter H has three lines.
Letter I is just one line with dots.
Letter J has a curve and a line.

Class activity:
Pupils trace letters on paper.
Then they write the letters on their own.

Evaluation questions:
Trace letter F.
Write letter G.
Which letter has three lines?

Summary:
We can write letters F to J.

topics.title: My name
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to trace their name.
The pupils should be able to write the first letter.

Introduction:
Last week we wrote many letters.
Today we write our names.

Content:
Your name is special.
The first letter of your name is capital.
We write names from left to right.

Class activity:
Pupils trace their name on paper.
Then they write the first letter on the board.

Evaluation questions:
Trace your name.
Write the first letter of your name.
How many letters are in your name?

Summary:
We can write our names.

topics.title: Revision and handwriting race
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write neat letters.
The pupils should be able to show their best writing.

Introduction:
This week we revise all we learned.
We have a handwriting race.

Content:
We write numbers 1 to 5.
We write letters A to J.
We write neatly in the lines.

Class activity:
Pupils write their best on paper.
Then they show their neat writing on the wall.

Evaluation questions:
Write the number 3.
Write the letter F.
Which writing is the neatest?

Summary:
We are all good writers.
